title: A 10.5mW Automotive Touch AFE IC Featuring Radiated EMI Reduction Based on Pipelined Dual-Frequency Modulation and Sine2 Waveform Shaping for CISPR 25 Class 5 Compliance
problem: Automotive touch-screen sensors must comply with CISPR 25 EMI standards while maintaining high SNR and frame rate, but typical driving signals (200-500kHz) radiate harmonics that violate emission limits; prior approaches (COM, high-voltage, PRP, FDM) either require FFT overhead or are ineffective at attenuating harmonics.
motivation: Touch-screen integration in vehicles demands EMI compliance (CISPR 25 Class 5) for safety; low-voltage, low-frequency operation reduces emissions but degrades SNR and frame rate, creating a fundamental design trade-off.
method: Pipelined dual-frequency modulation combined with sine2 waveform shaping in the AFE to reduce radiated EMI without FFT overhead; selective driving signal modulation attenuates harmonics while maintaining SNR and frame rate performance.
key_novelty: Sine2 waveform shaping combined with pipelined dual-frequency modulation achieves CISPR 25 compliance without FFT-based filtering, eliminating area and power overhead of traditional FDM approaches.
contributions: Pipelined dual-frequency modulation reducing harmonic radiation
Sine2 waveform shaping for effective harmonic attenuation without FFT
10.5mW total AFE power consumption achieving CISPR 25 Class 5 compliance
Maintained SNR and frame rate performance compared to prior low-frequency/low-voltage approaches

metrics.other: CISPR 25 Class 5 EMI compliance, maintained SNR and frame rate

baselines: Code-division multiple driving (COM), high-voltage driving, pseudo-random pulse (PRP), frequency-division multiple driving (FDM)
limitations: Specific SNR, frame rate, and harmonic attenuation dB values not provided; comparison with state-of-the-art solutions not detailed.
primary_theme: EMI-compliant automotive touch AFE via optimized waveform shaping
